*I’d hold shipment for one high-priority bug.*

*P1 — Renewal dates clamp against the wrong month* — `src/schedule.js:6–7`
The day is capped using the *source* month’s length, then used to construct a date in the *next* month. This both skips renewal months through JavaScript date overflow and loses the original anchor after short months.

Reproduced with anchor `31`:

| From | Expected next renewal | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| Jan 31, 2026 | Feb 28, 2026 | Mar 3, 2026 |
| Jan 31, 2028 | Feb 29, 2028 | Mar 2, 2028 |
| Feb 28, 2026 | Mar 31, 2026 | Mar 28, 2026 |
| Mar 31, 2026 | Apr 30, 2026 | May 1, 2026 |

Clamp against the *target month’s* length while retaining the supplied anchor. Add regression coverage for short-month entry, restoration to the original anchor, and leap years.

*Validation:* All 5 existing tests pass, but an additional calendar sweep found 94 failures across 2,604 anchor/month combinations for 2024–2030. Proration matches the documented calendar-month rule; I found no additional defects.

Reviewed `billing-anniversary` at `f73b00d` against `main` at `7f89e48`. No files changed.
